data.head: # Scope — 2026-11-14-auto-exploration (Auto-exploration, escher-0.3.0 · Epoch 4 — Determinism and exploration)

body:
Auto-exploration — breadth-first over available actions within a step budget; panics, refusals caught; each path an
owner-only replayable check, no shot; navigation a boundary fork (v030-09).

Capability `v030-09` (requirement): one command drives every available action breadth-first within a step budget,
catches panics and refusals, and records each path as a replayable check (intent §Findings 7, E2). Its acceptance as
route wrote it: one command, given a step budget, drives every available action breadth-first, reports each panic and
refusal it meets, and leaves each path as a recorded check that replays green.

- One exploration command over a held app: from boot, it enumerates the actions available on the screen, drives them
  breadth-first (each path re-reached from a fresh session, the frontier ordered by path length) until a step budget is
  spent, and returns a closed report.

- The available actions come from the driver's own readers, never a hand list: the `actions` reader
  (`Session::actions`, v030-06) and the schema's verb table (`VERBS`) — a verb exploration can drive is one the table
  holds and the actions answer offers on a node. [inferred]

- Every step runs as a validated call through the one run path (`Session::run`), as `Session::reach` does — no second
  executor. [inferred]

- A refusal met on a step is caught and reported by its closed cause; a panic raised inside a step is caught and
  reported as a closed word, the path that led to it kept; neither stops the exploration. [inferred]

- Each explored path is left as a kept check (the 2026-10-19 recording format, `Check`), owner-only (`0600` file in a
  `0700` launcher-named directory, the same refusal of a group- or other-open directory), holding no `screenshot`
  step, and replaying green through `Check::replay`. [inferred]

- Exploration reads the default seed alone (`DEFAULT_SEED`), as every driver session does today: no seed argument. A
  later seed argument is an addition to the command's arguments, with no rework of what this chunk builds (the
  operator's direction at take-up; F1 of `2026-11-14-seeded-randomness` stays the founder's and PROVISIONAL).

- Proven on the stand's served tasks in both layout modes, and on a fixture that panics in a handler and one that
  holds a refusing control. [inferred]

- Navigation: a step whose action would navigate the document (a link, a form submission to another URL) is a
  boundary fork — the founder's. Until he answers, the most conservative reading holds provisionally: exploration does
  not follow navigation (such an action is not driven, or the step is not taken) and loads nothing new. [inferred]

- Which carriers reach the command (in process only, a binary role like `coverage`, or a driver verb on the command
  line, MCP and the socket) is a boundary question; a new verb or role on a carrier is a widening — the founder's fork,
  the most conservative provisional until he answers. [inferred]
- No `screenshot` in an explored path; no pixel at rest.
- No new log field carrying content; a span, if any, holds fixed words and counts only.
- No panic path on untrusted input (the budget, the directory): refused as typed values.
- Not in scope: `drag` or any two-target verb's production, canvas virtual nodes, a seed on any carrier.

title: I3-adapt-0.3.0-for-canvas.md.txt
body:
# Adapting 0.3.0's planned work to the 0.4.0 canvas plans (the escher overseer's reconnaissance, 2026-10-29)

**Why.** The founder, 2026-10-29: «давай теперь сделай разведку чтоб понять возможно то что мы планируем делать сейчас
стоит адаптировать с учетом планов, чтоб не получилось что мы что то строим а в итоге прийдется полностью переделывать
изза новых требований». The 0.4.0 plans are in `canvas-and-node-graph.md`: virtual nodes inside a canvas, the canvas
observed as data, a `drag` verb, and pan and zoom through a transform.

**Read at `a6c6a37c7`**: `escher-0.3.0/requirements.md`, `working-route.md`,
`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/element_id.rs`, `snapshot.rs`, and `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs`,
`command.rs`, `wire.rs`. These are the overseer's reading of the code, not measurements.

## What already fits (no rework expected)
- **The snapshot is built from the accesskit tree** (`snapshot.rs:98`: «its id and role from that tree»). That tree
  carries non-DOM nodes natively, so a canvas's virtual nodes can enter it without a new carrier.
- **An action lands on a point.** `click` and `type` press the centre of the target's bounds
  (`execute.rs:360`, `:427-439`). A virtual node with bounds can be clicked the same way, as long as the canvas app
  hit-tests its own pointer events.
- **The wire is versioned** (`wire.rs:37`, `v3`), so a new verb is an additive, versioned change.

## Where 0.3.0 could build something 0.4.0 would have to redo
1. **The stable-id grammar** (`element_id.rs`). Today an id is an author key, an anchored path (`//`), a component path,
   or a document path (`/…`), all derived from DOM and vdom elements. A virtual node has no DOM element. If D2, B3,
   E2's recorded checks and replay store ids in this grammar, 0.4.0 needs a form for `{canvas element}` + `{virtual
   key}` that collides with none of the four. **Adapt in «The UI graph» (v030-05): reserve that form now (a separator no
   current id can hold), even if nothing produces it yet.**
2. **The node model of the UI graph and of «What can I do here»** (v030-05, v030-06). If the graph and the actionable
   list are keyed on a DOM element (`Target.node: NodeId`, `execute.rs:354`), a virtual node does not fit. **Adapt: key
   them on the agent-visible node (the accesskit node with its bounds), with an optional owner element, and let a
   handler sit on an owner element and serve sub-targets.** A canvas typically has one listener that dispatches inside.
3. **Verbs as a closed list in B3 and E2** (v030-06, v030-09). If «What can I do here» and auto-exploration hard-code
   `click`/`type`/`press`/`scroll`, adding `drag` (two points or a node plus a destination) means reshaping both.
   **Adapt: read the per-node verbs from the schema's verb table, and let the recorded-check step format carry verbs
   with more than one target, versioned.**
4. **Handler coverage** (v030-07) counts DOM listeners. A canvas's internal handlers are invisible to it. **Adapt:
   state that limit in its acceptance, so 0.4.0 extends it rather than redefines it.**
5. **Layout explained** (v030-11) reads Taffy and Stylo. A virtual node's place is the app's own. **Adapt: let its
   answer name the "placed by the app inside canvas X" case, so the field set is not closed.**
6. **Bundled fonts** (v030-14). Canvas text (`GlyphRun`) must draw from the same bundled fonts, or a canvas reads
   differently across hosts. **Adapt: in its acceptance, name canvas text as a reader of the bundled set.**
7. **Engine debts** (v030-04). The transform `visible_region` fix should be proven on a pan/zoom container like the
   node graph's (`canvas-and-node-graph.md`).

## What 0.3.0 should not take on
The canvas renderer itself, the CPU renderer's custom-paint gap, `drag`, and virtual-node production all stay in 0.4.0.
The adaptations above keep 0.3.0's shapes open; they add no 0.4.0 capability.

- A refusal met on a step is caught and reported by its closed cause; a panic raised inside a step is caught and
  reported as a closed word, the path that led to it kept; neither stops the exploration. [premise-corrected: no
  catch exists today — dioxus-core 0.7.10 and `Session::run` (`execute.rs:180-197`) hold no `catch_unwind`, so a
  handler panic unwinds to the caller; exploration adds the first catch, around one step, and drops that step's
  session]

- Each explored path is left as a kept check (the 2026-10-19 recording format, `Check`), owner-only (`0600` file in a
  `0700` launcher-named directory, the same refusal of a group- or other-open directory), holding no `screenshot`
  step, and replaying green through `Check::replay`. A step that panicked is never recorded (the session records a
  call once answered, `execute.rs:191-196`), so a panicking path's check holds the steps before it.

- Proven on the stand's served tasks in both layout modes, and on a fixture that panics in a handler and one that
  holds a refusing control.

- Navigation: a step whose action would navigate the document (a link, a form submission to another URL) is a
  boundary fork — the founder's (away: his forks to `founder-forks.md`, inputs#I1). Until he answers, the most
  conservative reading holds provisionally: exploration follows no navigation and loads nothing new. [premise-corrected:
  in a harness-built session no navigation provider is configured (`harness.rs:17-31`, `59-73`), so the document takes
  `DummyNavigationProvider` (`document.rs:507-509`) and a navigating action loads nothing; exploration drives such an
  action like any other, adds no provider and never switches documents]

- Which carriers reach the command (in process only, a binary role like `coverage`, or a driver verb on the command
  line, MCP and the socket) is a boundary question; a new verb or role on a carrier is a widening — the founder's fork,
  the most conservative provisional until he answers.

- The verbs exploration drives are read from the schema's verb table and the actions answer, never a closed list in
  exploration's own code, so a future verb (0.4.0's `drag`) is driven with no reshaping.

- The recorded-check step format can carry a verb with more than one target, and is versioned: a kept check states its
  format version, and a two-target step is an addition to that format, not a redefinition. [premise-corrected: the step
  format already carries any verb's arguments by their schema names (`recording.rs:115-127`, `426-428`), so a two-target
  step needs no change; it holds no version today (the opening record's keys are closed at `tool`, `arguments`,
  `recording.rs:402-410`), so this chunk adds one]

# Founder forks — 2026-11-14-auto-exploration (phase P4, 2026-11-14)

The founder is away. On the operator's directive (inputs#I1: «his forks (navigation is one) go to founder-forks.md, most
conservative provisional, no dialog»), no dialog is raised: each fork below stands on its first option PROVISIONALLY, and
the plan is built on it. Both forks name the playbook pattern `rul-izni57qv` (Boundary widening): every option but the
first ships a widening. His answer is appended below and snapped; an answer other than A is a later chunk's work.

## F1 — Which carriers reach exploration?
Exploration drives a held app breadth-first and leaves each path as a kept check. Today it would be reached:

- **A — In process only (Recommended, the provisional answer).** A Rust call, `escher_driver::explore`, used by tests and
  by in-process code that boots an app; no verb, role, argument, exit or span is added to the command line, MCP or the
  session socket. Why: it widens nothing, follows the start-in-a-state precedent (your C, inputs of that chunk), and a
  carrier can be added later as an addition, reusing the same entry. Trade-off: an agent over MCP or the command line
  cannot ask for an exploration yet.
- **B — A binary role, like `coverage`.** `escher-session explore <app> --budget <n> --record <dir>`: one process, a
  fresh in-process session per path, one stdout line of ids, closed words and counts. A boundary widening (a new role and
  answer on the command line).
- **C — A driver verb on every carrier.** `explore` the fifteenth verb, on the socket, the command line, MCP and in kept
  checks. The widest: a new verb, new argument kinds and a report answer on every ratified carrier.

## F2 — Does exploration follow navigation?
A step can navigate: a link click, Enter on a link, a form submission to another URL.

- **A — Follows none (Recommended, the provisional answer).** The held instance navigates only as its boot configured
  it; every harness-built session (the stand, the fixtures) has no navigation provider, so a navigating action loads
  nothing. Exploration drives such an action like any other, adds no provider and never switches documents. Why: no
  page, URL or file is loaded that the boot did not already load; nothing new crosses. Trade-off: a multi-page app is
  explored one document at a time.
- **B — Follows navigation within the app.** Exploration installs a navigation provider and explores the next document
  it names. A boundary widening: it loads documents the app's boot did not, and a navigation's URL becomes an input.

## The founder's answer
_(none yet — appended verbatim when it arrives, then snapped)_

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-11-14-auto-exploration · **Version:** escher-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-11-14T14:30:00Z

One in-process call, `escher_driver::explore`, takes a caller's boot and a step budget, drives every action the held
app offers breadth-first — each path re-reached on a fresh session through the one validated run path — and returns a
closed report: for each explored path its calls and how it ended (accepted and settled or not, refused with its closed
cause, a caught panic, or a re-reach that diverged). Given a recording directory, each path is left as an owner-only
kept check that replays green through `Check::replay`. No step is a `screenshot`, so no pixel rests anywhere. The verbs
come from the schema's verb table through the `actions` reader, never a list of exploration's own, and the call driven
for a node is the call `actions` judged (`call_naming`), so 0.4.0's `drag` is explored with no reshaping (inputs#I2,
inputs#I3). Exploration reads `DEFAULT_SEED` alone; a later seed argument is an addition — the seed already reaches a
run only through the caller's boot closure, so a seed argument maps into that boot with no change to what this chunk
builds (inputs#I1; architecture · decision/no-seed-on-carriers stays PROVISIONAL).

The kept check gains a format version: the opening record is written `{"tool":"start","arguments":{"app":…},"format":1}`
and read with an absent `format` as format 1, any other value refused `malformed`. The step format already carries a
verb with any number of id targets by their schema names (`recording.rs:115-127`, `426-428`); a unit test pins a
synthetic two-target verb's step round-tripping, so a two-target verb is an addition to format 1, not a new format.

The two boundaries are the founder's forks, written to `founder-forks.md` (inputs#I4) on the operator's directive and
held on their first option provisionally: F1 — exploration is in process only (no verb, role, argument, exit, span or
carrier is added); F2 — exploration follows no navigation (a harness-built session has no navigation provider,
`harness.rs:59-73` → `DummyNavigationProvider`, `document.rs:507-509`; exploration adds none and never switches
documents). Per architecture · decision/validated-commands-only, security-plan · decision/one-validation-path-for-every-carrier,
test-plan · decision/recorded-checks-replayed-as-tests and obs-plan · decision/driver-spans-carry-no-content.

1. **The kept check's format version** — `packages/escher-driver/src/recording.rs`. Add a public constant
   `CHECK_FORMAT: u32 = 1` (re-exported). `opening(app)` writes the opening record with `format` after `arguments`.
   `opening_app` takes the opening record's closed keys `tool`, `arguments`, `format`; `format` absent reads as 1,
   present it must be the integer 1, anything else (another number, a string, a negative, a float) refuses the check
   `Malformed` holding nothing of the bytes. `Check` keeps no new field (one format is read). Update the crate-level
   and `Check::from_bytes` docs. Keeps arch S5 (no `unwrap`), S6 (docs).

2. **Its unit tests** — `packages/escher-driver/src/recording_tests.rs`: the written opening record's bytes hold
   `"format":1`; a check with no `format` key reads (the pre-format form, as the committed checks were); a check with
   `format` 2, `"1"`, `-1` and `1.5` is refused `Malformed`; a synthetic `VerbSpec` with two `Id` arguments (built in
   the test, not added to `VERBS`) has its call written by `record_of` and read back by `call_of` with both targets in
   schema order. Each table states its row count (tests S4).

3. **The committed checks re-recorded** — `tests/blitz-tests/checks/counter-cli.json` and `counter-mcp.json`, written by
   the binary through `examples/seven_guis/tests/flows/record_checks.sh` (the gate entry below), never by hand; the
   seven_guis `recording` test then reads them byte-equal (test-plan · decision/checks-byte-equal-to-recording).

4. **`call_naming` shared** — `packages/escher-driver/src/actions.rs`: `call_naming` and `target_verbs` become
   `pub(crate)`, unchanged otherwise, so exploration builds the very call `actions` decided.

5. **The exploration** — new `packages/escher-driver/src/explore.rs`, opening with `//!`, public items `///`
   (arch S6), no log site, no span of its own (each driven call leaves its own `command` span), no print, no env read:
   - `StepBudget` — a whole number from 1 to `MAX_EXPLORE_STEPS` (10,000), built by `StepBudget::new(u32) ->
     Option<StepBudget>` (0 and past the bound `None`): the most acting calls an exploration runs, every re-reach step
     counted (security-plan · decision/no-panic-on-call-input).
   - The verbs explored are the instance verbs `actions` reads (`target_verbs`) less any verb whose result fields hold
     an image — selected by the table's own result field `png` (`VerbSpec::fields`), never by a verb's name — so
     today `click`, `type` and `scroll`, and a future id-taking verb with no image joins with no change here.
   - `explore(boot: impl FnMut() -> Result<Session, SessionError>, budget: StepBudget, record: Option<&Path>) ->
     Result<Exploration, SessionError>`: the frontier starts at the empty path; for each path taken off the front, a
     fresh session from `boot` (recording into `record` when given, `Session::recording_into`), its prefix's calls run
     through `Session::run` in order (a prefix call whose acceptance differs from the first run, or that panics, ends
     the path `Diverged { step }`), then its last call run inside `std::panic::catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(..))`.
     A path that ends accepted (settled or not) and whose screen — the digest of `harness().doc.snapshot().to_text()`
     after the step — no earlier path reached is expanded: one child per `actions` node (snapshot pre-order) per
     explored verb (table order), every reading, accepted or refused, so a refusal is met by running its call. A
     refused, panicked or diverged path is never expanded. The run stops when the frontier is empty (`exhausted: true`)
     or the next path would pass the budget. A panicked step's session is dropped (or, if the open question below
     shows a drop that panics, forgotten — a stated limit). A boot error ends the exploration with it; a recording
     directory refused (`RecordDirNotPrivate`) ends it before the first boot's step.
   - `Exploration { paths: Vec<ExploredPath>, steps: u32, exhausted: bool }`; `ExploredPath { calls: Vec<Call>,
     ending: PathEnding }`; `PathEnding::{ Accepted { settled: bool }, Refused(Cause), Panicked, Diverged { step: usize
     } }` — closed words, indices, `Call`s (ids and the fixed in-bound values `call_naming` gives) and bools; no panic
     payload, no `NodeId`, no screen text, never logged or printed (security-plan · decision/driver-outcomes-never-logged).
     A path's kept check is `check-{n}.json`, `n` its index + 1 in a directory that held no check (the recorder's
     smallest-free-number rule, `recording.rs:236-257`); a panicked path's check holds its steps before the panic (a
     call is recorded once answered, `execute.rs:191-196`).
   - Split into module-level functions so none reads over the cognitive ceiling of 15 (architecture ·
     decision/cognitive-complexity-ceiling).

6. **Its unit tests** — new `packages/escher-driver/src/explore_tests.rs`, a `#[cfg(test)] #[path]` child (arch S4):
   `StepBudget::new` at 0, 1, 10,000 and 10,001 (4 rows asserted); the explored verbs read from `VERBS` are `click`,
   `type`, `scroll` and `screenshot` is not among them; a synthetic verb table holding an image field excludes that verb
   (the selector reads the field, not the name). The executor paths are the stand check's: the driver crate builds no
   held instance (test-plan · decision/driver-executor-integration-tested).

7. **The public surface** — `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs`: `mod explore;` and re-export `explore`, `StepBudget`,
   `MAX_EXPLORE_STEPS`, `Exploration`, `ExploredPath`, `PathEnding` and `CHECK_FORMAT`; the crate doc's module list gains
   one paragraph: what exploration does, in process only, its seed and navigation readings.

8. **The stand check** — new `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_explore.rs`, `//!` naming the behaviour; every test in both
   layout modes on the stand's bundled font, no sleep, no wall-clock read, failure messages naming a mode, a task and an
   index only (arch S1–S2, tests S2–S5, obs S1); its two fixture pages stay in this file, one reader each (arch S3), each
   control keyed by an HTML `id` with an accessible name (layouts S1–S2, a11y S1):
   1. `every_served_task_is_explored_within_its_budget` — the six served tasks, each through its stand boot (the Timer
      with `timer_step`), budget 40: the exploration returns, `steps` ≤ 40, `paths` non-empty, every path's calls name
      only `click`, `type` or `scroll` (no `screenshot`), and the paths are the same on a second run (determinism).
   2. `the_counter_is_explored_whole_and_each_path_replays_green` (`cfg(unix)`) — the Counter, budget 200, a recording
      directory `0700` under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR`: `exhausted` reads true, a path clicking `counter-increment` ends
      accepted, every kept check reads through `Check::from_bytes` with `format` 1, holds no `screenshot` step and
      replays holding on a fresh session (`Check::replay(...).holds()`), and the directory holds one check per path.
   3. `a_refusing_control_is_met_and_reported_by_its_cause` — a fixture page with a disabled keyed button beside an
      enabled one: a path ends `Refused(Cause::Disabled)` on the disabled button and is not expanded; the enabled one's
      path ends accepted.
   4. `a_panicking_handler_is_caught_and_the_exploration_goes_on` — a fixture page with a keyed button whose `onclick`
      panics and a keyed button that counts: the panicking path ends `Panicked`, later paths still run (the counting
      button's path ends accepted after it in frontier order), and a session booted after the caught panic answers a
      snapshot (the open question's witness). Assert the fixture first: the panicking button is listed by `actions` with
      `click` accepted (arch history, 2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph's trap).
   5. `a_panicking_paths_kept_check_holds_the_steps_before_it_and_replays_green` (`cfg(unix)`) — the same page recorded:
      the panicking path's check holds no step of the panicking call and replays holding.
   6. `a_group_open_recording_directory_is_refused_with_nothing_written` (`cfg(unix)`) — a `0750` directory: the call
      returns `SessionError::RecordDirNotPrivate` and the directory holds no file.
   7. `the_budget_bounds_every_acting_call` — Cells, budget 25: `steps` reads exactly the acting calls run (counted by a
      boot wrapper that counts sessions and the paths' call lengths), never above 25, `exhausted` false.

9. **The capability statement** — `docs/capabilities.md`, by hand: a claim «a breadth-first exploration in process»
   naming `stand_explore`, and its limits: in process only (F1 provisional); follows no navigation (F2 provisional);
   no `screenshot` step; a panic payload never read; the std panic hook still prints a caught panic in a process that
   keeps it; `drag` and canvas virtual nodes 0.4.0's. No verb, cause or count moves, so
   `.github/scripts/test_capability_statement.py` reads it unchanged (architecture · decision/capability-statement-matches-schema).
- `packages/escher-driver/src/explore.rs` — the exploration
- `packages/escher-driver/src/explore_tests.rs` — its unit tests
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_explore.rs` — the stand check and its two one-reader fixture pages
- `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs` — the module, re-exports, crate doc paragraph
- `packages/escher-driver/src/actions.rs` — `call_naming`, `target_verbs` crate-visible
- `packages/escher-driver/src/recording.rs` — the format version written and read
- `packages/escher-driver/src/recording_tests.rs` — the version and two-target tests
- `tests/blitz-tests/checks/counter-cli.json` — re-recorded by the binary
- `tests/blitz-tests/checks/counter-mcp.json` — re-recorded by the binary
- `docs/capabilities.md` — the claim and its limits

The gates run the driver's unit tests, the new stand check, the existing checks that read kept checks (their reader
changes), the committed checks' regeneration and its byte-equal reader, the doc leg for the new public items, and the
local pre-push gate `fast` (fmt → clippy → workspace tests → CI scripts → embolden). No live leg: every check is an
in-process cargo target or a seven_guis process check that owns its host. No smoke entry: the test plan declares no
boot-smoke trigger paths and nothing launches an app or mints an id. The diff adds OS-conditional sites — the
`cfg(unix)` items of `stand_explore` — so the plan carries the operator's hygiene, push and CI entries; the CI entry's
note names the OS legs that witness them. The `coverage` (escher-driver's 97 % floor) and `stand-repeat` legs run in
CI, read through that entry.

  `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs`, `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/harness.rs`, `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs`.

- External inputs: inputs#I1 (the operator's directive), inputs#I2 (the founder's checklist), inputs#I3 (the
  reconnaissance, item 3), inputs#I4 (the founder's forks, held provisionally).

- A second executor or a direct harness input in exploration — every step is a `Call` through `Session::run`
  (architecture · decision/validated-commands-only).

- A list of verb names in exploration's code — the verbs come from `VERBS` through `target_verbs` and the image field
  (inputs#I3); a name appears in a test only.

- Reading the panic payload, installing or swapping a panic hook — a payload is page or app text, and a hook is a
  process-global side channel the driver library never takes (architecture · decision/driver-library-side-effect-free).
- A verb, role, argument, span, exit or carrier for exploration — F1 holds on A provisionally (inputs#I4).
- Installing a navigation provider or switching documents — F2 holds on A provisionally (inputs#I4).
- A new format number for a two-target step — the step format already carries it; format 1 stays (inputs#I2).
- Rewriting the committed checks by hand — the binary records them (`record_checks.sh`).
- A seed argument — a later addition through the caller's boot (inputs#I1).

- Equality the capability needs: a path's prefix re-run on a fresh session from the same boot reads the same screens,
  because the stand boots are deterministic (architecture · decision/stand-readings-same-on-every-ci-os) and every step
  runs through the same `Session::run` (`execute.rs:180`); `Diverged` reports where that fails rather than masking it.

- Two clicks on one point with no `advance` between read as a double click (a11y history, 2026-10-18-one-virtual-clock);
  a path that clicks one target twice explores that double click, replayed identically — not a defect.

- Right after a `scroll` the shown overlay scrollbar takes a pointerdown in its band as a thumb drag (design history,
  2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar): a click path after a scroll on Cells may read accepted with no change; reported as read.

- An option of a closed select is refused `covered` until its select opens (architecture ·
  decision/closed-select-options-covered): the flight booker's options' paths end `Refused(Covered)`, expected.

- Cells' `actions` reads 678 nodes at boot (`ACTIONABLE_AT_BOOT`, stand_actions) × 3 explored verbs: the budget, not
  the frontier, bounds a Cells exploration.

- The std panic hook prints a caught panic's message to stderr in the process that catches it; a test harness captures
  it per test. In escher-session no exploration runs (F1 A).

- Open question from research: a session whose VirtualDom unwound mid-handler is dropped; if that drop panics (a
  double panic aborts), forget it instead and state the leak as a limit — test 8.4 is the witness.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Standard Contracts — `escher_driver::explore` (in process; the budget, the
  report's closed endings, a fresh session per path, verbs from `actions`, the image-field exclusion); and the kept
  check's opening record gains `format` 1 (architecture · contract/kept-check/opening-record); absence rows, PROVISIONAL
  on F1 and F2: exploration on no carrier, and exploration follows no navigation, each under `rul-izni57qv` (the
  pattern named; held on the operator's directive as delegate for the founder, inputs#I1, inputs#I4 — the wrap's full
  escalation stands).

- Expected amendments (wrap): security-plan §Input Validation and §Data Protection — the budget bounded and refused
  as `None`, the report holding closed words, indices and calls only, never logged; a kept check's `format` read
  strictly (security-plan · decision/recorded-check-strict-reader); the explored paths' checks under the same owner-only
  medium.
- Expected amendments (wrap): test-plan §5 — `stand_explore` the check of exploration, and a kept check's format.

- Expected amendments (wrap): obs-plan §4 — exploration adds no span; each driven call leaves its own `command` span;
  a caught panic still runs the process's hook (obs-plan · contract/escher-telemetry-panic-hook/previous-hook).
